correctness.rationale: For a mixed support each old arc forces the sole cyclic completion; consistency of the new arcs is equivalent to monochromaticity on the full selected rectangle. One-shore supports give the orientation-independent term. Free amalgamation and homogeneity give existence and type uniqueness over the named base. Balancing the two groups per row and the six pair/color groups separately gives the coefficientwise lower bound by discrete convexity; the latter group sizes sum to b+2t, where t counts constant columns. Strict convexity at z=1 and strict increase of the balanced-six total as its sum increases rule out t>0 at equality. When t=0, the six groups are in bijection with the six nonconstant columns. Their q/q+1 counts and balanced row sums are both required in the frozen claim. At size two the extra patterns must be complementary, and size four is the complement case. At size three each of the six row/color choices excludes exactly one triple, and no two of those exclusions coincide; this gives 14. Independent enumeration of the 64 possible sets of extra patterns confirms (1,6,3,14,3,6). The upper bound counts all mixed supports; requiring all 2-by-1 and 1-by-2 rectangles to be monochromatic forces the constant matrix (with the second condition vacuous for b=1). The z=1 substitutions and mixed-count order ratio follow directly. The supplied finite checker and its recorded output were inspected, not executed; the all-b conclusion follows from the proof.

value.rationale: The named one-point spectrum tests what the orientation adds beyond the underlying graph. Three rows are structurally meaningful: each nonconstant column has exactly one monochromatic row pair, while a constant column has three. This yields an exact equality family with nontrivial remainder constraints, simultaneously minimizes every support size for all b, and shows an exponential spread in the orientation-sensitive part. The value lies in the minimum and its full classification, not the trivial count obtained by orienting everything the same way.
